_comment: ProGramerly - the data and preset registry. Antwerp Designs | Ionity (Pty) Ltd | AEDI - Policy 986 AED. Every set the local model is allowed to read, and every standing question it answers from them. This file is the boundary: services/dome.js will only serve a set that is listed here, and the brief handed to the model is built only from listed sets. `class` is how a figure must be reported - measured came off a sensor or a scan on this machine; catalogue is curated data shipped with the app; manifest is a pinned digest; state is what this install has recorded; computed is derived from the others and never presented as a reading.

classes.measured: Read from a sensor, the OS or a live scan on this machine, now.
classes.catalogue: Curated data shipped inside the application.
classes.manifest: A pinned record - sizes and SHA-256 digests.
classes.state: What this installation has recorded about itself.
classes.computed: Derived from other sets. Never a reading.

datasets.name: Sensor tree
datasets.shape: groups[] -> sensors[] { name, type, value, unit }
datasets.about: Every temperature, fan, controller, load, voltage, power and clock the driver exposes, grouped by the chip that owns it.

datasets.name: Fan channels
datasets.shape: channels[] { label, parent, role, rpm, duty, controllable }
datasets.about: Tachometers paired with the controllers that drive them, plus every temperature source available to a curve.

datasets.name: Fan curve profiles
datasets.shape: profiles[] { name, points[], minDuty, stopBelow, commandedDuty }
datasets.about: Curves designed in this application, each evaluated against the live temperature so the commanded duty can be compared with the measured one.

datasets.name: Live metrics
datasets.shape: { cpu, mem, disks[], net, temp, uptimeSec, host }
datasets.about: The same sample the tray and the deck paint from: CPU load and clock, memory, every volume, throughput and package temperature.

datasets.name: Volumes
datasets.about: Each mounted volume with used percentage and free bytes.

datasets.name: Memory state
datasets.about: Installed, free and standby-list memory - the last being memory Windows counts as free while behaving as though it is not.

datasets.name: Lighting devices
datasets.about: Controllers reachable on the OpenRGB protocol, if its server is running.

datasets.name: Privilege state
datasets.about: Whether this process holds an administrator token, and what it is running on.

datasets.name: Registry fix set
datasets.shape: fixes[] { id, name, symptom, status, action }
datasets.about: The curated set of Microsoft-documented repairs, each with the symptom it addresses and its state on this machine.

datasets.name: Port listeners
datasets.about: What is bound to the ports a development machine contends over.

datasets.name: Resolved toolchain
datasets.about: Each expected tool resolved to the binary that actually answers on PATH, with its version.

datasets.name: Doctor findings
datasets.shape: items[] { id, title, status, detail, fix }
datasets.about: The last diagnostic pass - what was checked, what was flagged, and the action that clears each finding.

datasets.name: Reclaimable space
datasets.about: Caches and temporary trees, sized before anything is removed.

datasets.name: Catalogue items
datasets.shape: items[] { id, name, group, desc, profiles[], dependsOn[], win, mac }
datasets.about: The curated software graph this application installs from - the largest data set it ships.

datasets.name: Catalogue groups
datasets.about: How the catalogue is organised, and how many items sit in each group.

datasets.name: Installed set
datasets.about: Catalogue ids this installation has installed on this machine.

datasets.name: Tool payload pins
datasets.shape: programs[] { name, file, expectedBytes, sha256, available, integrity }
datasets.about: The Ionity tools shipped with this build, pinned by byte size and SHA-256, with their verification state.

datasets.name: Repositories
datasets.shape: repos[] { name, path, branch, ahead, behind, dirty, stack }
datasets.about: Git working copies under the development root and their state.

datasets.name: Development root
datasets.about: Where projects, environments and clones live.

datasets.name: Local models
datasets.about: Models held on this machine and which are resident in memory now.

datasets.name: Inference endpoints
datasets.shape: endpoints[] { id, name, port, up, models[] }
datasets.about: Local inference services that are actually listening.

datasets.name: GPU devices
datasets.shape: gpus[] { name, vramTotalMb, vramFreeMb, utilPct, tempC, fits }
datasets.about: Accelerators present, free VRAM, and what will fit in it.

datasets.name: Environments
datasets.about: Virtual environments, conda environments and Node versions available.

datasets.name: MCP configuration
datasets.about: Model Context Protocol servers configured for the clients on this machine, and whether each binary is still installed.

datasets.name: Official link registry
datasets.about: The Ionity and AEDI link registry, plus the package and AI endpoints the application depends on.

datasets.name: Sync state
datasets.about: The scheduled code-base sweep: whether it is on, what it covers, and when it next runs.

datasets.name: This registry
datasets.shape: datasets[] { id, name, class, about, available }
datasets.about: The registry itself - every set in reach, and which are available on this machine right now.

datasets.name: Analysis presets
datasets.shape: presets[] { id, name, scope, question, reads[] }
datasets.about: The standing questions below.

presets.name: State of the machine
presets.question: Read the sets provided and give me the state of this workstation in three short paragraphs: what is healthy, what is under pressure, and the single thing most worth doing next. Quote real figures and say which set each came from.

presets.name: Thermal and airflow brief
presets.question: Assess the thermal and airflow position of this machine. Name the hottest sensors, whether the fans answering them are spinning and controllable, and whether any stored curve would command a different duty than the one measured. Be specific about channel names.

presets.name: Which curve should I run
presets.question: Given the fan channels, the temperature sources and any stored curves, recommend a curve shape for the main CPU channel: the points, a minimum duty, and whether a stop-below threshold is safe here. Explain the reasoning in two sentences, then give the points as a list.

presets.name: Disk pressure and reclaim
presets.question: Report disk pressure by volume, then list the reclaim candidates largest first with their sizes. Say plainly how much would be freed and what would be lost by removing each.

presets.name: Toolchain gaps
presets.question: Compare what the catalogue offers with what is installed and what actually resolves on PATH. List the gaps that matter for a working development machine, most important first, with the catalogue id for each.

presets.name: Repository standing
presets.question: Summarise the repositories: which have uncommitted work, which are behind their remote, and which look abandoned. One line each, path included.

presets.name: Model fit for this machine
presets.question: Given the accelerator, free VRAM and system memory, say which of the installed models will run comfortably and which will fall back to the CPU. Recommend one model to add for coding work and justify it with the memory figures.

presets.name: Integrity and privilege
presets.question: Report the integrity state of every pinned tool, the privilege this process holds, and anything listening on a development port that was not started deliberately. Flag anything that fails its pin.

presets.name: Explain the last scan
presets.question: Explain the diagnostic findings in plain language: what each one means, whether it matters on a development machine, and the order to address them in.

presets.name: What can you see
presets.question: List every data set you can currently read on this machine, grouped by class, and state in one line each what you could report from it. Name the sets that are unavailable and why.
